{
    "body": "## What happened

Soak #2 (formal Direction Episodes Phase-3 acceptance, EngineDreckDave/3106, 2026-09-02T15:48:15.807Z-16:48:15.807Z) FAILed `--direction-gate` on "zero unclosed episodes" — one episode (`dmtka4ans4`, `project_stalled`) stayed open for the entire remainder of the window (30+ min, tagged by `metrics.mjs` as a DEAD-CONSUMER) with **zero further attempts, from any layer, to resolve it**.

Traced from the raw ledger, not guessed at:

1. `15:56:57.977Z` — `dmtka4ans4` opens (`project_stalled`) for the bot's ongoing `chopTrees` project.
2. `15:58:21Z` / `16:00:37Z` — the decider tries the Andy/LLM path twice (its designed 2-attempt cap), gets `!digDown(...)` then `!moveAway(...)`, both correctly unmappable/discarded, and gives up on this episode per its own retry-cap doctrine (`giving up on episode dmtka4ans4 after 2 unusable Andy replies`).
3. The underlying `chopTrees` project (unrelated to those two failed dispatch attempts) travels ~250 blocks and lands at (-17,108,3), where it starts failing `kit_missing` (the `excursion` kit tier — torches/food/weapon, exact missing item unconfirmed) repeatedly: 16:00:05, 16:00:37, 16:01:39, 16:03:39, then a clean 5-minute cadence for the rest of the window (16:08:39, 16:13:39, 16:18:39, 16:23:39, 16:28:39 — 9 occurrences inside the graded window alone, continuing past it).
4. Every one of those cycles runs `RESTOCK -> IDLE -> PROJECT -> IDLE`, clockwork-regular, **no thrash whatsoever** — RESTOCK genuinely tries first every time, can neither withdraw nor produce what's needed, and stands down gracefully per #37's own doctrine (a real capability, not a bug). PROJECT then retries the identical `chopTrees` call anyway and immediately re-fails the identical kit gate.
5. Because `dmtka4ans4` never closed, agenda's own reopen-backoff (by design — see the `setProject`/`keepNext` doctrine and its sibling reopen-cooldown logic) never opens a *fresh* `project_stalled` episode on top of an already-open one for the same bot. So all 9+ repeats of the identical failure after the decider's give-up generated **zero further direction-episode activity** — no rule, no LLM, no driver ever looked at it again.

## Why this is a real gap, not a tuning miss

Every individual piece behaved exactly as designed:
- RESTOCK's graceful stand-down when nothing is withdrawable/producible (#37) is correct behavior, not a bug.
- The decider's 2-attempt-then-give-up cap (avoiding infinite LLM spend on a persistently-unmappable episode) is correct behavior, not a bug.
- Agenda's reopen-backoff (not re-opening a fresh episode on top of an already-open one) is correct behavior, not a bug.

The **composition** of all three correct pieces produces an episode that can rot open indefinitely with nothing watching, the moment the decider's one LLM attempt happens to land on unmappable Andy replies (which #68's own soak-2 FEEDBACK entry notes is common — Andy's usability rate has historically run ~25-40%). This is exactly the acceptance criterion soak #2 was built to test, and it genuinely failed it.

## Suggested directions (not mutually exclusive)

1. **Escalate rather than silently give up.** When the decider exhausts its Andy attempts for an episode, instead of pure silence, either retry after a cooldown (conditions may have changed — RESTOCK might succeed on a later attempt if the bot wanders near a producible resource), or mark the episode with a distinct `state` (e.g. `decider_exhausted`) that a driver/monitor can actually see and act on, rather than it looking identical to a healthy `needs_direction` episode that just hasn't been picked up yet.
2. **Give repeated identical failures their own `why`.** A project failing the *same* `kit_missing` gate N times in a row is a more specific, more mappable signal than the generic `project_stalled` — Andy (or a rule) might have a much better shot at something like `kit_deadlock` than at the generic stall, and it would also make a rule-of-twice promotion possible (right now nothing repeats consistently enough to promote, because the underlying `why` never changes shape).
3. **Feed RESTOCK's own repeated-failure count into the direction layer.** RESTOCK already knows it stood down empty-handed 9 times in a row at the same position for the same reason — that's a strong, cheap, zero-LLM signal that something needs a driver's attention, independent of whatever the decider concluded about the episode.

## Evidence

Full timeline, exact timestamps, and gate output in FEEDBACK.md (2026-09-02, "Soak #2 (formal Phase-3 acceptance) graded"), verdict file `bench/gates/direction-soak2.json`.

Filed per team-lead's standing doctrine (an unfiled same-day finding with concrete evidence gets rediscovered expensively later) rather than left as a soak grading footnote.

like a human player. First attempt: soak #4's combined verdict.

PLAYER — tidy builds, honest chat manners, fair play, no scars, respected
claims — and cooperate with others both ALONE and in BIG COORDINATED EFFORTS

allied fleets). Coordination at scale is a first-class capability, not a

that can do everything a good human player needs, ALONE, engine-driven (may use
parallel development). PHASE 2 — only once phase 1 is solid, make players

wherever possible. When something HAS to go through an LLM, do it — but then

with other bots from the same framework, with bots from other frameworks, and
with human players — and that can build bases, trading stations, farming,
mining shafts, claims (respected, never destroyed), food production, hunting,

grace) that keyed on the label's mere *presence*, not its actual semantic ("is a driver watching
and answering right now"). Same rot class as "assumed-false ≠ verified-false" — presence-of-metadata
gates must name the semantic they check (`driven`, not `owner`).

  --title "same-remedy-repeats-across-positions escalation — decider reassigns identical remedy from each new frozen position" \
  --label "bug,priority-high,owner-engine-dev-3,phase-1,robustness" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened (soak #4, MampfManfred, corrected finding — 2026-09-03)

The soak bot never held a tool the entire hour: every wood-gather attempt FROZE (ledger `frozen`
wedge events). The direction layer itself worked correctly — episodes opened and closed 10/10, zero
unclosed — but the decider kept **reassigning the identical remedy (`chopTrees`)** from each new
position the bot ended up at after a freeze, and the bot re-froze there too. Full verdict context:
#90 (soak #4 comment), SCOREBOARD.md "SOAK #4", TODO.md item 5c.

(Corrects an earlier same-day mis-read of this data as a "busy-but-unproductive rung detector" /
TOOL-sword-loop finding — re-traced from the ledger, the actual mechanism is the wood-gather freeze
loop described above, not a busy-rung blind spot.)

## Why the existing dedup doesn't catch it

`decider.js`'s frozen-repeat dedup (#97 item 3, `1e11afd`) skips an identical dispatch **from a
frozen position** — but it keys on position. Once the bot relocates (even trivially, to an adjacent
tile) and freezes again, the position key changes, the dedup doesn't fire, and the decider hands out
the same remedy class (`chopTrees`) again. The bot can cycle through N different positions, freezing
at each one, with the decider treating every one as a fresh, un-repeated situation.

## Design direction

N same-remedy failures **across positions** (not just at one position) → escalate: either a bigger
relocate (further than the freeze-recovery radius) or a different remedy class entirely (not another
`chopTrees` dispatch). This needs a counter keyed on (bot, remedy) rather than (bot, position) —
pairs with the held #95 follow-ups (episode-rot escalation is the same "the decider's single-shot
retry logic has no memory across attempts" class of gap).

## Live specimen available

MampfManfred, post-grade, is a NATURAL "frozen while gathering wood" specimen still on disk — worth
diagnosing live (R2 tooling) before/alongside the design work, per TODO 5c.

## Gates

Soak #5 (the next human-bar attempt) is gated on this landing alongside #109 (decider driver-grace
latency fix) — both TODO items 4b/5c.

Cross-ref: #90 (soak #4 verdict), #95 (episode-rot escalation, same "no cross-attempt memory" class),
#109 (decider latency fix, same decider.js lane).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011bT5tbJqCPah3pNidP5op3
EOF
)"

input.command:
gh issue create \
  --title "soak #4 host reboot at T+56 — post-hoc grade; window-truncation annotation for graders" \
  --label "priority-low,owner-engine-dev,phase-1.5,robustness" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened

A clean systemd reboot hit the host at 2026-09-03 08:46:12Z, T+56:30 into soak #4's pre-registered
07:49:42.327Z–08:49:42.327Z window (~3.5 min before the natural end). Bot, inspector, and lead
session all died. The ledger's last record is 08:46:06Z.

Graded per the pre-registered fallback ("the ledger persists — grade with those exact bounds"):
server restarted from its saved world, a fresh inspector (`Trail4Insp2`, DECIDER_EXCLUDE, no
--agenda) run against the exact staged command and original window bounds. Verdict: #90 (soak #4
comment), SCOREBOARD.md "SOAK #4", gate files `bench/gates/*-soak4.json`.

## The gap

The fallback worked (grading proceeded, verdict stands), but nothing in the grading tooling
(`bench/humanbar4.mjs`, `trail.mjs`, `metrics.mjs --direction-gate`) currently **annotates** a gate
file when the underlying window was truncated by an infra event rather than running the full
pre-registered duration. A future grader (human or automated) reading `bench/gates/humanbar4-soak4.json`
cold has no signal that ~3.5 min of the window never happened — it just looks like a clean full-hour
run that happened to end at :49:42.327Z minus the reboot gap.

## Ask

A machine-readable annotation on the gate file (or a sibling `*-notes.json`) when a soak's actual
data window is shorter than its pre-registered window: truncation cause (here: host reboot), the
actual vs. registered end timestamp, and whether the fallback grading rule was invoked. Low priority
— this soak's verdict is already correctly caveated in prose (SCOREBOARD.md, FEEDBACK.md, #90), this
is about making that caveat survive into the gate JSON itself for future automated re-reads.

Cross-ref: #90 (soak #4 verdict, the caveat this formalizes), #52 (instrument integrity, same
curator lane).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011bT5tbJqCPah3pNidP5op3
EOF
)"

# IDLE_TRIGGER_SPEC — Direction Episodes

**Status:** FINAL synthesized specification (2026-09-02). SHIPPED (2026-09-02): all four phases
built and live-verified — see FEEDBACK.md's Phase 1/3 entries and felcrew-mcp#68.

**VERSION NOTE:** this spec was written against agenda v20, landing Direction Episodes as
v21. Before it landed, engine-dev-3's #89 (digOut/ascendToSurface) claimed v21 first for the
unrelated ESCAPE rung — Direction Episodes shipped as **v22** instead (a number, not a
functional change), and the follow-on setProject/nextProject ruling (§1.1i) bumped it once
more to **v23**. Nothing below keys off the literal version number — every consumer
(`bench/fixtures/agenda-direction.js`, `metrics.mjs`) checks for `A._directionCheck`'s
existence instead, exactly so a version bump elsewhere in the file never invalidates this
spec's own text. Read every "v21" below as "the version that ships Direction Episodes,
whatever that turns out to be."
**Problem (Felix):** bots idle too often; nothing triggers the LLM when a toolchain finishes, fails, or a bot has no direction. Measurement is half the request: idling must become a number.
**Base design:** Direction Episodes (failure-first, judge winner 146/144/131 summed, 2-of-3 judges' pick), with grafts from the events-minimal design (log marker, /state observability, rules-before-LLM, poll-as-sweep) and the queue-ahead design (promotion placement + hygiene, gap_ms cross-check, contradiction alarm). Every judge must_fix is resolved in §8.

---

## 0. Architecture in one paragraph

"Needs direction" becomes **latched, level-triggered state inside agenda.js** (`A.direction`), opened by deterministic edges read off ladder state — never off raw movement, so a 200-block haul can never false-fire. At most ONE open episode per bot; the episode holds until something fills the project slot (a driver, the fleet decider, a promoted queued-next, or deterministic self-recovery), and the close stamps `latency_ms` at the source. Consumption is **pull** (GET /state polling + a stdout log marker for push-like driver wake); dispatch is race-safe via an episode-id compare-and-set. A 1-deep `A.nextProject` slot, staged at decision time (the decider always answers current+next), makes steady-state completions promote at zero tokens and zero gap — episodes then fire only when the queue is empty. One shared **decider.js** daemon serves the driverless fleet: rules.json first (zero tokens), one Haiku call on a rule miss, every decision logged for rule-of-twice conversion. The engine spends zero tokens; the LLM is the metered exception the codicil demands.

Notation: file line anchors below are against the current live files (agenda.js v20 @ 1043 lines, runner.js @ 1057, telemetry.js @ 501, metrics.mjs @ 477, bots-llm/planner.js @ 530). Anchors are the *current* lines; after edits, find by the quoted code, not the number.

---

## 1. Engine changes, per file

### 1.1 agenda.js — v20 → v21 (~90 lines) — lane: engine-dev-3

**(a) State.** Extend the `A` literal (lines 104–117):

```js
direction: {
  state: 'ok',                 // 'ok' | 'needs_direction' | 'cooldown'
  episode: null,               // {id, why, openedAt, detail}
  prevLvl: 'none',             // central edge detector's last composite level
  lastProductiveAt: 0,         // set to now() at install (reinjection grace)
  reopenAt: {}, reopenCount: {},   // per-why escalating reopen backoff
  opened: 0, closed: 0, promoted: 0, byWhy: {},   // UNCONDITIONAL counters (#38 witness 1)
},
nextProject: null,             // 1-deep queue: {skill,args,tool,restockFloor,repeat,stagedAt}
```
Bump `version: 21`.

**(b) Constants** (near the existing block, lines 39–102):

```js
const DIRECTION_IDLE_WINDOW_MS = 120000;   // E2: undirected-idle window
const DIRECTION_STALL_MS       = 180000;   // E3a: stalled-project window
const DIRECTION_BARREN_RUNS    = 3;        // E3b: consecutive zero-yield repeat runs
const DIRECTION_REOPEN_MS      = [30000, 60000, 120000, 300000];  // same shape as STAND_DOWN_MS
```

**(c) `dirEmit(op, fields)` helper** next to `note()` (lines 121–129). Does exactly two pushes, each try/catch-wrapped like `note()`'s S.log mirror:
1. stdout marker: `console.log(new Date().toISOString() + ' AGENDA_EVENT ' + JSON.stringify({ev:'direction', op, ...fields}))` — lands in `logs/<name>.log` via spawn.sh:36's `>> "logs/$NAME.log"` redirect; this is the driver wake signal.
2. ledger: `const m = M(); if (m && m.emit) m.emit('direction', Object.assign({op}, fields))` — the SAME proven-live path the rung-transition `note` uses at line 965 (`m.emit('note', ...)`), NOT an optional guard into a phantom sink (#38/#54-R2 lesson).

<teammate-message teammate_id="engine-dev" color="yellow" summary="File issue: EAT/EAT_CRITICAL rungs can permanently deadlock a starving bot">
Please file a tracker issue (felsenuboot/FelsenBerry, repo felcrew-mcp renamed) for a bug I confirmed live in agenda.js. Requesting HIGH severity — it's a starvation-death risk for the current role-less fleet shape (#88).

**Title**: EAT/EAT_CRITICAL can permanently deadlock a role-less starving bot — FOOD rung can never preempt them

**Body**:

Confirmed live on a throwaway test bot (HungrigHeinz, OWNER=engine-dev, DECIDER_EXCLUDE=1, --agenda, role-less, 25599, ~347 blocks from the only other bot on that server; run #6/GammelGerhard on the separate 25600 race server untouched). Full writeup with logs and /eval evidence in FEEDBACK.md, entry starting "### 2026-09-03 engine-dev — task 3: FOOD rung hunts and eats (confirmed), but EAT/EAT_CRITICAL can PERMANENTLY DEADLOCK...". Test ran on skills v62/agenda v30 at commit 872aa07 — AFTER #113 (shared FOODS allowlist) and #114 (huntAnimals species widening) both landed, so this is not those bugs recurring.

**What happens**: `EAT` (agenda.js, prio 4, `fire: food<=17 && foodCount>0`, `clear: food>=19`) and `EAT_CRITICAL` (prio 2, same shape at food<=6) both call `eatInline()` directly, bypassing the `__skills` task system, and unconditionally return `'ate'` regardless of whether anything was actually eaten. `choose()`'s owner-latch (`if (owner && !safeClear(owner,s) && demanded.prio >= owner.prio) return owner`) keeps the current owner in place whenever nothing MORE urgent is firing — it never re-checks whether the owner's OWN `fire()` is still true. The first time EAT or EAT_CRITICAL eats its last food item without reaching `food>=19` (routine — one raw beef/mutton rarely refills a badly-starved bot that far), it's stuck: `fire()` is now false (foodCount=0, can't be re-selected) but `clear()` is also false (nothing left to eat, never releases). `FOOD` (prio 6.5 — the only rung that can actually fix this by hunting more) is LOWER priority and can never preempt a stuck higher-priority owner.

**Reproduced twice in one live session**: first hunt succeeded (a cow, ate the beef, exactly #108's acceptance case) — but food fell back down before recovering to 19, EAT got stuck for ~35s of dead HP-draining time, and only escaped because an UNRELATED nightfall SHELTER trigger (prio 2.5) happened to preempt it. gh issue create \
  --title "cook/smelt skill — bots eat raw meat; no furnace path for food" \
  --label "enhancement,priority-medium,owner-engine-dev-3,phase-1" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Follow-up from #113/#108's live-testing session (FEEDBACK.md ~09:42Z, "TODO 5e" entry, part c)

Flagged during live verification of #113/#114 (checked `./task.sh list` and `producer.js` for
any cook/smelt-food skill — **none exists**; `producer.js` only smelts logs into charcoal for
torch fuel, `restock` only withdraws from depot chests).

Today this is not a blocker: the excursion kit's food gate counts raw meat fine (per #108/#113's
raw-meat allowlist), so a role-less racer that hunts raw meat can already satisfy the kit gate
without cooking it. But if that gate — or any future one — ever specifically wants a COOKED item,
a bot with raw meat in hand has **no legal `setProject` path** to turn it into one. A
`smeltItem`/`cook` skill (furnace + fuel + raw-food recipe, the same shape as `producer.js`'s
existing charcoal-smelting path) is real, missing infrastructure for any role-less bot past this
point — a human player cooks meat as a matter of course, and bread/farmed food already needs an
established wheat farm this bot doesn't have.

## Fix shape

Not designed in detail here — flagged as a real gap, not proposed as a specific implementation.
Likely shape: mirror `producer.js`'s existing log→charcoal smelting flow (furnace lease,
fuel-slot management, output collection) for raw-meat→cooked-meat, dispatchable via `setProject`
like any other skill.

Cross-ref: #113 (the raw-meat allowlist fix this gap sits downstream of), #108 (the FOOD rung
this eventually feeds).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011bT5tbJqCPah3pNidP5op3
EOF
)"
